items.prompt: A signed-in admin sends PATCH /api/crm/contacts/c1 with body { "enrichmentFields": { "email": "a@b.co" } }. What does the route return?
items.answer: 400 with the error No valid fields to update
distractors: 200 with success true, and the email is changed
400 with the error enrichmentFields required
404 with the error Not found for that contact
items.explanation: FIELD_MAP is an allowlist of enrichment columns (position, website, social links, description, phones); email is not in it, so updates stays empty and the route returns 400 before any write. The allowlist is what stops mass assignment here.

items.prompt: A user with role user PATCHes a valid enrichment field on contact c9, which they neither created nor are assigned to. What comes back?
items.answer: 404 Not found, as the scoped updateMany matches zero rows
distractors: 403 Forbidden, as the route checks the contact owner before writing
200 success, since any signed-in user may enrich
401 Unauthorized, as the role is too low for writes
items.explanation: contactScopedWhere adds OR [assigned_to, createdBy] for the user role, so updateMany updates zero rows and tryScopedUpdateContact returns false. The route then answers notFoundOrForbiddenResponse, which is a 404: it does not reveal that the contact exists.

items.prompt: Which accounts does accountReadScopeWhere let a user with role manager read?
items.answer: Each account whose deletedAt is null, whoever owns it
distractors: Only the accounts the manager is assigned to or has created
Every account, including the ones that were soft-deleted
Only accounts that a member of the team is watching
items.explanation: For admin and manager the scope is just { deletedAt: null }: all live accounts. Only the user role gets the extra OR over assigned, created and watching. Soft-deleted rows stay hidden for every role.

items.prompt: A user with role user calls the updateAccount server action with the id of an account they have no relation to. What happens?
items.answer: The update goes through, with no ownership check made
distractors: It returns Unauthorized, since the user role is checked
It throws AuthorizationError from assertCanWriteAccount
It matches no row, so it returns Failed to update account
items.explanation: updateAccount calls getSession() and then prisma.crm_Accounts.update({ where: { id } }) with no scope. assertCanWriteAccount exists in lib/authz/scopes/crm.ts but is not called here, which is the read/write asymmetry the guide points out.

items.prompt: formatNumber("INV-{YYYY}-{###}", 2026, 12345) runs on a busy series. What string does it return?
distractors: Its last three digits, so INV-2026-345
A truncation to 123, as in INV-2026-123
A cap at 999, which yields INV-2026-999
items.explanation: The {###} placeholder is replaced with String(counter).padStart(3, "0"). padStart only adds zeros up to the width; it never truncates or caps a longer value, so the full counter 12345 appears.

items.prompt: A YEARLY series has counter 41 and currentYear 2025. consumeNextNumber runs on 2026-01-03 (UTC). Which counter value goes into the new number?
items.answer: 1, after the counter is reset for the new year
distractors: 42, because resets happen only on a manual run
0, which is the value that the reset writes back
41, because the year change skips one increment
items.explanation: currentYear 2025 differs from the UTC year 2026 and the policy is YEARLY, so counter is set to 0 and then incremented to 1; the series row is saved with counter 1 and currentYear 2026.

items.prompt: Both API keys resolve, but the contact being enriched has no email. What status does the enrichment row end with?
items.answer: SKIPPED, with No email on contact as its error
distractors: FAILED, with NO_API_KEY stored as the row error
RUNNING, left there when the function returns
COMPLETED, with an empty enrichment result
items.explanation: With keys present the row is first set to RUNNING; the contact is then loaded and, because contact.email is empty, the row is updated to SKIPPED with "No email on contact" before any agent call.

items.prompt: The contact already has a website and an empty mobile_phone. The agent returns values for website and mobile_phone. Which columns does the worker write?
items.answer: mobile_phone alone, as website was already set
distractors: website and mobile_phone, overwriting both
website only, since it is the first returned
Neither column, since one of the fields already had a value
items.explanation: The merge loop copies an enrichment value only when isFieldEmpty(currentValue) is true for that column. website keeps its existing value and mobile_phone is filled. The guide notes the lost-update window this leaves for user edits made meanwhile.

items.prompt: A send already has status bounced. Resend then delivers an email.delivered event for it. What does the webhook route do to the row?
items.answer: Nothing changes, as delivered needs the status to be sent
distractors: It sets status to delivered and clears the stored error message
It rejects the event with a 409 status conflict response
It sets status to delivered but keeps the error
items.explanation: The email.delivered case updates the row only inside if (send.status === "sent"). A bounced send is left as it is, and the route still answers { ok: true }. email.bounced, by contrast, is written unconditionally.

items.prompt: RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not set in the environment. Resend posts a correctly signed event. What does the route answer?
items.answer: 401 Invalid signature, even for a correct signature
distractors: 200 ok, as signature verification is skipped without a secret
500, because createHmac throws when it is given no key
400, since the body cannot be parsed
items.explanation: verifyResendSignature returns false when either the signature header or the secret is missing, so the route answers 401 before parsing anything. There is no development bypass.

items.prompt: A recipient clicks the same unsubscribe link a second time, a week after the first click. What happens?
items.answer: The page shows again, and unsubscribed_at keeps its date
distractors: A 404 page, since the token was consumed by the first click
The page shows again, and unsubscribed_at is set to now
A 400 page saying the link has already been used once
items.explanation: The send is found by its unsubscribe_token; the update runs only if unsubscribed_at is empty, so the first date is kept. Either way the route returns the 200 HTML page. Tokens are not consumed.

items.prompt: A user has 10 API tokens: 2 are expired and none are revoked. They call generateApiToken once more. What happens?
items.answer: A new token is created, as only 8 of them count as active
distractors: It throws Maximum 10 active tokens allowed per user
The oldest expired token is deleted and then reused
A new token is created, and the cap is raised to 11
items.explanation: The cap counts tokens with revokedAt null AND (no expiry or expiresAt in the future). Expired tokens do not count, so activeCount is 8 and the new token is created. Nothing is deleted.

items.prompt: An admin demotes a logged-in manager to user. The manager's session cookie is still valid. When does their next server action see the new role?
items.answer: On its next requireAuthenticated call, via a DB read
distractors: Only after the session expires, up to 7 days later
Only after the 24-hour session refresh is triggered
Only after they sign out and sign in again by OTP
items.explanation: requireAuthenticated takes only the user id from the session, then re-reads the Users row and maps its role on every call. The role is never cached in the session, so the demotion applies immediately, at the cost of one query per call.

items.front: Why does tryScopedUpdateContact use updateMany with a scoped where instead of check-then-update?
items.back: The ownership scope lives inside the WHERE clause, so authorization and the write are one atomic statement: no time-of-check/time-of-use window. count === 0 means "not yours or not there", which the route maps to 404 so existence is not revealed.

items.front: Why is consumeNextNumber only safe inside a Serializable transaction?
items.back: It reads the series counter, maybe resets it for a new year, adds 1 and writes it back: a read-modify-write. Two concurrent issues could read the same counter and produce duplicate numbers unless the caller (issue-invoice) runs it with isolationLevel Serializable. The invariant is owned by the caller, not the helper.

items.front: Why are MCP API tokens hashed but provider API keys encrypted?
items.back: Tokens are only ever verified: store SHA-256 of nxtc__... and compare hashes, so a DB leak reveals nothing usable. Provider keys (OpenAI, Firecrawl) must be sent to the provider again, so they need reversible AES-256-GCM encryption. Hash what you only verify, encrypt what you must reuse.
